intended_object: The subgroup of universal norms of A^G: the elements of the total invariants A^G lying in the image of the norm N_{G/V}: A^V → A^G for every open normal subgroup V of the profinite group G. It is viewed as a closed subgroup for the compact topology chosen by `LevelCompact` (inferred from the docstring, the name and its use as the kernel of the projection to the Tate limit).
explanation: The carrier is `universalNormSubmodule A (fullOpenNormalSubgroup G)`. By definition this is the intersection, over open normal V ≤ G, of the ranges of `relativeNorm A ⊤ V`. That map sends x in A^V to the sum of g·x over a transversal of V in G, and the library proves the result is independent of the transversal. So the carrier is exactly the intersection of the norm images N_{G/V}(A^V) inside A^G, the standard universal-norm group. Closedness follows because each range is the continuous image of a compact space in a Hausdorff space, and an intersection of closed sets is closed. The library proves this subgroup equals the kernel of the projection from A^G to the inverse limit of the degree-0 Tate groups (`compactUniversalNormClosedSubgroup_eq_ker`), which matches the textbook picture. The profinite setting is the natural one for universal norms, and the underlying submodule is already defined for any compact group. Packaging it as a `ClosedAddSubgroup` is what the later additive quotient construction needs. Mathlib has no notion of universal norms.
